author: Inside Edition
description: The FBI says a missing teenager, allegedly being held at a captor's house, was rescued because of a video game. According to the criminal complaint the teen was found at the home of a man in Huntington, Oregon, after connecting with a fellow gamer playing Among Us. Their conversation transferred to social media where the teen claimed they were missing and being held against their will according to the filing. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Teen Held Captive Asked For Help in Online Video Game: FBI

author: Inside Edition
description: A jury found Russell Brand guilty of rape. His wife, who had accompanied the actor to court in London, found herself besieged by reporters after the verdict. The 51-year-old Brand was immediately whisked away in a prison transport van. Prosecutors have called Brand a "ruthless sexual predator." Following the verdict, police released Brand's interrogation tapes, in which he refused to answer questions and insisted he only read from a prepared statement where he said he "never engages in non-consensual sexual activity."
title: Russell Brand's Interrogation Tapes Released Following Guilty Rape Verdict

author: Inside Edition
description: Actor and comedian Russell Brand was convicted Thursday in a London court on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The judge said Brand will be sentenced to prison. He was found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. Brand, 51, was acquitted on two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. The allegations, made by six women, spanned a 10-year period beginning in 1999.
title: Actor Russell Brand Convicted of Rape, Sexual Assault in London

author: Inside Edition
description: Army veteran Ryan Walton still has nightmares, paralyzing depression and smothering guilt. Seventeen years after Nidal Hasan opened fire at the Fort Hood base in Texas, Walton still agonizes – could he have done more on that harrowing November day? Walton walks Inside Edition Digital's Deborah Hastings through that awful day, and explains why Hasan's execution will bring no closure to him.
title: There Is No Closure For Fort Hood Shooting Survivor As Killer's Execution Nears

author: Inside Edition
description: The Peruvian National Forestry and Wildlife Service says an estimated 3,000 tarantulas were discovered in the luggage of three passengers bound for Germany. The hairy arachnids were hidden inside socks. They included tarantulas at every stage of development – from eggs to fully grown adults. Several different tarantula species were among the cluster. It's believed that the various-colored creatures are sought by illicit animal collectors.
title: 3,000 Tarantulas Found In Smugglers' Socks

author: Inside Edition
description: Actor Nicolas Cage told an audience at Comic Con that he's quote, "a little bit homeless." That's because his Malibu house was severely damaged by a sinkhole in early September. Not only has he been unable to move back in, he says he's been living in hotels over the past nearly two months. Cage made the comments during a panel discussion at the Los Angeles event on Halloween. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Nicolas Cage Says He's 'A Little Bit Homeless' Since House Damaged By Sinkhole

author: Inside Edition
description: We're getting a new look at the site where a Learjet60 crashed earlier this week. Drone footage of a neighborhood in Palm Beach, Florida shows a crater in the earth, where most of the plane hit. The impact tore a hole in the road, but thankfully missed several homes only yards away. Nine people died in the accident. The NTSB says a final report on the crash and its causes may take more than a year to complete.
title: Drone Footage Of Learjet Crash Site Shows Crater

author: Inside Edition
description: Workers with Bear Valley Electric Service in California had an unusual service call when they were asked to rescue a great horned owl.
title: Utility Workers Rescue Owl Stuck In Power Lines #shorts
